title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Risk Factors: dependence on third-party manufacturers and the GlobalFoundries Wafer Supply Agreement (p24)
key_points: Under the amended WSA, GlobalFoundries provides a minimum annual capacity allocation for 2022–2025 and AMD has corresponding annual wafer purchase targets.
If AMD misses an annual wafer purchase target, it must pay GF a portion of the difference between actual wafer purchases and the target.
AMD was obligated in 2022 and is obligated in 2023 to pre-pay GF certain amounts for those wafers.

AMD does not have long-term commitment contracts with some third-party manufacturing suppliers and obtains some services on a purchase-order basis, with no guaranteed minimum quantity beyond existing purchase orders.
AMD states the WSA amendment no longer includes exclusivity commitments and gives full flexibility to contract with any wafer foundry.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Overview: FY2022 results context (p43)
key_points: FY2022 net revenue was $23.6 billion, up 44% from $16.4 billion in FY2021.
